To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) we introduce a differential geometry based sampling technique that, given any DGN, produces a uniform distribution of samples on the DGN manifold; (ii) our technique does not require retraining of the DGN and does not require labels; (iii) our technique produces a more uniform sampling of faces, and reduces gender bias in FFHQ, compared to the state-of-the-arts.
MaGNET is a simple and effective technique that produces samples from DGNs that are uniformly distributed over the learned manifold without retraining the model.

(i) we introduce MaGNET, a differential geometry based sampling technique that uniformly samples from DGN manifolds without requiring retraining, (ii) we prove that MaGNET produces a uniform sampling distribution on the DGN manifold, and (iii) we demonstrate the effectiveness of MaGNET on a variety of datasets and DGN models
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: {\em how to produce samples that are uniformly drawn from the manifold learned by a DGN without retraining?}
the question: {\em Can we sample from a DGN without retraining, such that the samples are distributed uniformly on the learned manifold?
the question of how to obtain uniform samples from a DGN manifold.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our technique is the first to produce samples that are {\em uniformly} distributed on the learned data manifold.
MaGNET is a novel and effective technique for generating samples that are uniformly sampled from the manifold of DGNs.
MaGNET is the first technique that allows for uniform sampling from the manifold learned by a trained DGN, without requiring any re-training.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, MaGNET is a simple yet effective technique to obtain a uniform distribution of samples on the manifold learned by any trained DGN without retraining.
we develop a sampler, MaGNET, that produces samples that are uniform on the manifold, regardless of the training data distribution.

MaGNET is a general-purpose, easy-to-implement technique that can be applied to a broad range of DGNs, and that it is capable of producing samples that are uniform on the learned manifold, and hence, are free from the artifacts of the training set.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MaGNET provides a simple, yet effective way to sample from DGNs without retraining.
MaGNET enables a new paradigm for data augmentation and anomaly detection by sampling uniformly from the manifold learned by DGNs.
MaGNET can produce a uniform distribution on a manifold learned by any DGN, regardless of the training data distribution, which is of independent interest for a variety of applications.
